To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
scheduled restart SGD (with momentum) improves the generalization performance of DNNs and converges faster than SGD with momentum, and that this is true for both small and deep networks.
SRSGD significantly accelerates training of DNNs, with better generalization and faster convergence than other state-of-the-art SGD variants.

(a) NAG with a time-varing momentum is not suitable for SGD due to its accumulation error; (b) scheduled restart SGD (with increasing momentum) improves convergence and generalizability of SGD; (c) SRSGD significantly outperforms SGD in terms of both convergence and generalizabilty; (d) SRSGD is especially beneficial for deep neural networks
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new NAG-type scheme for SGD that improves convergence and generalizes well in practice.
the design and analysis of a new NAG-based algorithm for training deep neural network.
a new momentum scheme that is both theoretically and empirically motivated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SRSGD is the new state-of-the-art SGD method, and it is the method of choice for training DNN models.
SRSGD improves both the speed and accuracy of training DNNs and is particularly effective for deeper and larger networks.
SRSGD is a new NAG-like algorithm for training DNN with accelerated convergence and improved generalization, which is a significant advance over the state of the art.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SRSGD is the first NAG-type algorithm for SGD with inexact gradients that is guaranteed to converge and achieves better convergence and generalization than SGD.
SRSGD achieves a faster convergence rate, higher accuracy, and lower computational cost in training DNN models.
SRSGD is a new NAG-like method for training deep neural nets with a schedule to stabilize the momentum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the momentum in SGD can be improved by a simple restart schedule, which can be easily incorporated into the training of DNNs.
, for training DNN models, NAG is not a good choice but SRSGD is.
SRSGD, with its simple design and easy implementation, can be used as a drop-in replacement for SGD and its variants for training DNN models.
